item.title: Kode 1.1.0
item.description:
Language servers, a minimap, Find File and navigation through places.
## Language servers
Kode talks to the language server of each language (LSP), found on your shell's PATH: clangd for C, C++ and Objective-C, and servers for Python, Rust, Go, JavaScript/TypeScript, QML, Swift, Bash, Lua, Java, Kotlin, YAML, JSON, HTML, CSS, Markdown, CMake, Dockerfile, Terraform and TOML.
- **Problems as you type.** A wave under each error or warning, its message where the pointer rests, and the counts in the status bar; a click there lists them and goes to one. clangd gets your build folder's compilation database. - **Quick fixes (⌥↩).** The server's fixes and refactorings at the caret, as Qt Creator's Alt+Return; one undo step. - **Go to Definition (F2, ⌘-click).** ⌘ over a name shows it as a link. **Switch Header/Source (F4)**, as in Qt Creator. - **Completion.** As a word starts, after "." or "->", or on ⌃Space; keep typing to filter, Return or Tab to accept. Includes the server adds come in the same undo step. - **Semantic highlighting.** Types, fields, locals, parameters and macros in C and C++, and QML's types, ids and bindings, in Qt Creator's colors. - **What the server is doing** (starting, analyzing, indexing) shows in the sidebar's footer. - **Settings ▸ Language Servers.** Turn them off, add folders to look in, set clangd's threads (one by default), add your own server for any language, and see what was found — or press and hold a missing one to copy its install command.
## Navigation
- **Find File (⌘K)**, as Qt Creator's Locate: a field in the middle of the window and the folder's files whose name matches, best first, each with its path. Also from the magnifying glass in the sidebar. - **Back and Forward go through places**, not only files: where you edited, clicked on another line or jumped from (a definition, Go to Line), as in Qt Creator.
## Editing
- **Brackets and quotes come in pairs.** Typing the closing one steps over it, Backspace in an empty pair takes both, and Return after "{" adds the "}" two lines down with the line between indented. - **A minimap** beside the text (View ▸ Show Minimap): click a line to center it, drag to scroll. - **Re-indent on save re-indents only the lines edited** since the last save; Edit ▸ Re-Indent (⌃I) still re-indents the selection.
## Large files
- **Large files open in the background.** From 2 MB on, the file is read and decoded off the main thread: the window says "Opening…" and stays responsive. - **A jump far down a large file is colored at once**, from a guess until the highlighting from the top gets there. - **Opening takes less memory**: opening 100 MB peaks at 495 MB instead of 782 MB.
## Changes
- **Text fields in macOS's filled style** in the find bar, Go to Line and Settings. - **The find bar has more room**, and its match count is a badge on the Find field's corner. - **Settings pages scroll** when taller than the window. - **Open, Open Folder and Save As start in your home folder** instead of the root of the disk.

item.title: Kode 1.0.3
item.description:
A small release for the sidebar.
## Changes
- **Move to Trash asks first.** The sidebar confirms before moving a file or folder to the Trash; Delete (or ⌘Delete) on the selection asks the same. - **Keyboard shortcuts in the sidebar**, shown in its right-click menu and working while the file tree has the focus: Open (⌘↓), Rename (F2), Move to Trash (⌘Delete), Copy Path (⌥⌘C) and Reveal in Finder (⌥⌘R). Cut, Copy and Paste (⌘X, ⌘C, ⌘V) act on the selected file, as in the Finder.

item.title: Kode 1.0.2
item.description:
A fix release.
## Fixes
- **Renaming in the sidebar** ends with Return (keeping the new name) or Escape (keeping the old one), names with spaces included; Return no longer goes on to open the file, and clicking elsewhere in the tree ends the rename. - **Files that are not text** (images, archives, binaries) open in the app macOS uses for them instead of in the editor. - **Bracket matching** skips brackets in comments and strings: a `)` inside a string no longer pairs with the `(` of the code around it.

item.title: Kode 1.0.1
item.description:
A fix release, and the first one that updates itself.
## New
- **Updates.** Kode looks for a new release once a day, downloads it in the background and installs it when you quit. **Kode ▸ Check for Updates…** checks right away; **Settings ▸ Updates** turns the automatic checks off and picks the channel (stable, or stable and beta). 1.0.0 had no updater: install this release by hand once, later ones arrive on their own.
## Fixes
- **Each folder has its own session.** The files a folder's window had open are saved when it closes (and on quit) and reopen with that folder only; a folder opened for the first time starts empty, and Kode launched without a folder opens one empty window instead of every file from last time. - **Make Default** asks macOS for the common code types only, and skips those Kode already opens, so it no longer asks for a hundred extensions one by one.
